about: MUTATING — run the DECLARED trim of the build node's two filesystems once, now, and put its own record on this packet (infra/forge/trim-build-node.sh; backlog 30a6bf39). Asked for and AUTHORISED by David, 2026-10-07: he ran the w-1 hand trim a second day running on the condition that the agent can do it itself in future, and this verb is authorised only by his own release of its held trust-boundary car — a release run by an agent session is not that authorisation. WHAT IT DOES: through the forge's ops_kubectl door, `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/boss-node-trim` in namespace boss-node-maintenance, so the pod is the scheduled CronJob's own template (train #989, daily at 12:40 UTC) and nothing this verb or its script wrote; it waits for that Job, prints the pod's own output — fstrim's bytes per mount, each NVMe's discard counters before and after, its closing OK or RED — and deletes the Job it made. NO PARAMETER: no node, path, image, namespace or Job name comes from the packet (the name is a fixed prefix and the UTC second), and the script refuses any argument. WHY IT NEEDS NO PASSKEY, which is the tree's own line (CLAUDE.md, Diagnosis: reads and bounded reclaims are mechanical, destructive-by-policy actions are not): (1) it can create ONE pod spec and no other — the bound is not this verb or its script but the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy node-maintenance-holds-one-workload, which admits a Job there only when its pod IS the trim pod (the image digest, the script byte for byte, two read-only host directories, one capability), whoever sends it, so an edited or subverted copy of this door could still only start one more of that pod; (2) what that pod does is a reclaim — fstrim tells the drive which blocks the filesystem ALREADY holds free, deletes no file and changes no byte a reader can see; (3) the same pod already runs unattended every day, so this adds an hour of the day, not a capability; (4) a plan would have nothing to render — there is no argument and no choice in it — and the hand act it replaces was far wider (`privileged: true` with the whole of /var mounted, in kube-system). This is a precedent for the PROCESS, as the verbs README asks, not a loosened default: a verb that creates any OTHER cluster object, or one whose object is not bounded at admission, earns no passkey-free door from this one. IT REFUSES, CREATING NOTHING (exit 78): when the policy's binding is absent, does not list Deny, names another policy, or carries a matchResources or a paramRef; when the policy it names is absent or its failurePolicy is not Fail; when the CronJob is absent (the namespace has not converged); when the CronJob is SUSPENDED (`.spec.suspend: true` is the in-cluster stop switch on the trim, and this verb does not run past it); when the CronJob on the server differs from the runner's checkout on what the script compares — one container, its image, its script byte for byte, activeDeadlineSeconds, backoffLimit, parallelism and completions; when any Job there is unfinished or any pod there is not terminal (the CronJob's own run, or another of these). WHAT IT DOES NOT COMPARE: the rest of the pod template (command, security settings, volumes, node selection) and the policy's own rules — the policy judges the pod at the create, and the line the script prints before the create says what was compared and that the rest was not. IT DELETES ONLY ITS OWN JOB: by name, and only while that name still carries the uid its create answered; never by a label. A create that does not answer success gives no uid, so nothing is deleted after one, and the name is read back before anything is said: no Job there is FAILED and says this run made none; a Job standing there is FAILED naming it and its uid, not removed, because it cannot be proven this run's; a read-back that cannot be made is CANNOT ANSWER, naming the Job to look for. OUTCOMES: exit 0 and the effect line only when the Job completed, the pod exited 0, the record names both mounts trimmed and closes OK, and the Job read back gone; exit 1 FAILED with the cluster's reason — the API server's refusal (admission), a pod that never started (image pull, unschedulable; judged after 180 s rather than at the deadline, because a pull that cannot succeed never fails a Job by itself), the Job's deadline, the pod's exit code, or this verb's own wait; exit 4 CANNOT ANSWER when the cluster could not be read — before the create nothing was made, after it the outcome is said to be UNKNOWN, never failed and never ok. A run killed at this timeout still removes its Job (the script's EXIT trap). NOT CLOSED: the in-flight check and the create are two calls, so a scheduled run starting between them gives two of the admitted pod at once. TIMEOUT 2400: the Job's own activeDeadlineSeconds (1800, read by the script from the manifest) plus 120 s for the controller to say so, plus the door's first-time image pull and the removal's read-back; ops_runner is one pass at a time, so a long trim holds every other request for the forge until it ends, and `boss ops --wait` gives up at 15 minutes while the packet stays the record. Pinned by crates/core/boss-testing/tests/trim_build_node_sh.rs.
effect: ^trim-build-node: OK — Job [a-z0-9-]+ completed and its pod exited 0; its record names .+ trimmed and closes OK, with [0-9]+ discard-counter line[(]s[)] before and [0-9]+ after; Job [a-z0-9-]+ removed [(]read back: NotFound[)]$
